title: "Zhihui Jun" has launched the consumer-level Qiyuan Q1 and T1 robots in cooperation with Swancor New Materials, with a unit price ranging from 20,000 to 30,000 yuan. Would you buy one?
key_facts: On 20 Sep 2026 Qiyuan Robotics, a consumer-grade embodied-intelligence brand of Swancor Advanced Materials, released two humanoid robots, Qiyuan Q1 and Qiyuan T1; shipping in order of orders from 1 Oct 2026.
Prices: Q1 19,999 yuan, Q1 Explorer Edition 26,999 yuan, T1 19,999 yuan, T1 Pro 29,999 yuan.

Q1: about 88 cm tall and 15 kg, foldable into a bag; T1: about 100 cm and 16 kg, switches between a wheel-foot humanoid form and a four-legged form. The 'world's first' descriptions are the company's.

Swancor is a specialty-materials company (resins, wind-turbine blade materials) that Zhiyuan took over in 2025; Peng Zhihui ('Zhihui Jun'), chairman and Zhiyuan Robotics co-founder, fronts the robot brand.
First-half 2026 report: revenue 803 million yuan (up 2.42%); net loss attributable to shareholders of 167 million yuan versus a 29.9 million yuan profit a year earlier, mainly due to robot R&D.
Advance payments from Q1 and T1 pre-sales reached 210 million yuan, which is not yet revenue until delivery.
36Kr compares rivals Unitree R1 (from 29,900 yuan) and Booster K1 (5,999 US dollars overseas, aimed at labs and competitions).
quote_evidence: On September 20, Qiyuan Robotics, a consumer-grade embodied intelligence brand under Swancor Advanced Materials, officially released two humanoid robots, Qiyuan Q1 and Qiyuan T1.
The net profit attributable to shareholders was -167 million yuan, turning from a profit of 29.9 million yuan in the same period last year to a loss.

However, advance payment is not equal to actual revenue, and can only be converted into revenue and profit after actual delivery, but this data shows that Qiyuan Robotics currently has no shortage of order popularity.
why_it_matters_hint: A cheap consumer humanoid is pushing the entry price toward 20,000 yuan, but the launch is three weeks old and the parent company is loss-making.
